edition.locus: Baehrens GCS 33 Comm. Cant. Liber II 10

source_text: Fulcite me floribus, stipate me malis, quia amore langueo. Sinistra eius sub capite meo, et dextera illius amplexabitur me. Adiuro vos, filiae Hierusalem, per capreas cervosque camporum, ne suscitetis neque evigilare faciatis dilectam, quoadusque ipsa velit. Hucusque Liber Secundus primam seriem lemmatorum a Nigra sum per fasciculum et botrum et lectulum usque ad adiurationem contexuit; sequentia in proximis tipis.
pass_a_gloss: Prop-up me with-flowers, heap me with-apples, because with-love I-languish. Left-hand of-him under head my, and right of-him will-embrace me. I-adjure you, daughters of-Jerusalem...
pass_b_english: [[Stay me with flowers, heap me with apples, for I languish with love. His left hand under my head, and his right hand will embrace me. I adjure you, O daughters of Jerusalem, by the gazelles and stags of the field, not to raise or awaken love until she please >> Bible:Song of Songs 2:5-7]]. Thus far the Second Book has woven its first series of lemmas from I am black through the bundle and the cluster and the couch as far as the adjuration; what follows will come in the next tips.
